findings.title: Third receipt worker stop refusal does not gate journal closure or hash
findings.evidence: HeldProtocol.close closes its socket, joins only remaining original deadline and raises while worker remains alive. native-call catches that refusal but continues fsync, context-manager journal close and unconditional ownershipJournal hfile. A receipt worker blocked in persistOwnership/regular-file fsync can retain write ownership while parent closes/reuses the file and hashes it. Immutable stat checks do not establish writer stop acknowledgement. Injected FakeWorker stayed alive, close refused, and caller source continuation was verified.
findings.requiredChange: Make receipt-worker ownership/stop acknowledgement explicit. Only retire/close/hash its journal after positive writer-stop acknowledgement; on unresolved writer retain unclosed evidence without hashing or reusing its descriptors. Bound protocol cancellation/close access too; qualify actual delayed-writer/start/interruption cases in a new frozen subject.

findings.title: Supervise pre-reap failures return without exact child closure
findings.evidence: After guest release and supervised_pid installation, oh_arm_deadline failure and oh_exit_held/channel/deadline failures return78 directly. Caller only reports shared state, munmaps and exits; oh_abort_unwaited exists only for oh_parent_release failure before supervise. Thus an exact fork child can remain live/unreaped/orphaned on these paths, while host eventually waits only for direct loader parent. This is refused output, not normal-path false acceptance, but the claimed bounded exact child failure cleanup is incomplete. WNOWAIT success does not cover all error/early-return paths.
findings.requiredChange: Track unreaped/exit-held/reaped/uncertain child state and alarm target ownership explicitly. On pre-reap failure use bounded exact-owned child cleanup with alarm target permanently retired before any potentially reaping cleanup wait. Never signal numeric PID after reap/uncertain ownership. Persist child closure or explicit unclosed state; handle waitid/ACK/EINTR/timer failure and timeout edges in deterministic then actual fixtures.

findings.title: Fallible peer close precedes durable direct-child PID publication
findings.evidence: After Popen returns, peer.close executes before assigning r.pid and saving attempts. If that close raises, cleanup has a local proc but saved/terminal row need not contain its PID; this loses durable handle identity on the failure boundary. Pure source ordering control verified the exact statement.
findings.requiredChange: Assign and durably publish proc.pid immediately after successful Popen return, before fallible endpoint cleanup/controller setup, while retaining one safe direct wait and explicit publication refusal.
